name: Casting off — Cra-Zi Landing
open: Lines off. Forty fares booked for Nowhere. Three days. It is always three days.

name: The Hippo Shallows
open: Brown backs surfacing in the shallows, and the channel narrowing to something a piano could touch both sides of.

name: The Narrow Cut
open: Two walls of black rock and a bend you cannot see past. No reverse. We're going in.

settle_stages.text: A steam launch on her side in the mud, listing hard, boiler still faintly hissing. Nobody has ever come back for her.
The Calliope is down to her rail now. Stack still standing. Still, faintly, venting.
A stub of stack and some birds. You have to know where to look, and you do.

name: Ilostmi Mine
open: Dead end. The adit is a cul-de-sac and the Ginny will not back out. The only way home is the way you came — you turn her with the helm while you still have way on, or the wall turns her for you. There is ore if you get out clean.
brief: She will not reverse. Almost every beat belongs on the helm. A joke is a luxury. The buckets will not turn the boat.

station_copy.steer: Helm over. No reverse — you are turning her with what way she has left. The wall is still there.
station_copy.wrench: You go below. The wall does not care that you are oiling something.
station_copy.bail: You hand out buckets in a hole with one exit. The water goes down. The boat does not turn.

name: The Reach
open: Open water. The chart is generous about this stretch, in wording it clearly did not read back.

name: The Snag Field
sub: The chart does not mention a fence
open: Timber in the channel, laid down like a fence somebody forgot to take in. You will duck. They will look at the wrong thing.

name: Crocodile Bend
open: The chart marks this stretch CROCODILE. The water is empty. The passengers came for teeth. They have opinions about the lack of teeth.

name: The Old Race
sub: The mill is gone. The water is not.
open: A mill race with the mill long gone. The water still thinks it has a job, and it is doing that job at you.

name: The Unnamed Shrine
sub: A landing. A name that isn't on the chart.
open: A stone landing and a shrine to a name that isn't written down. They want a photograph of something they cannot spell.

name: Knight Falls
open: There it is. Nine feet of water falling 108 inches. Forty passengers who paid for a legend.

station_copy.bail: This expedition is going underwater, fast.
station_copy.steer: The falls are not a channel. You keep her pointed downstream. The gauge eases. You are not parked.
station_copy.wrench: You go below during the advertised bit. They came for a waterfall.

name: The Floating Market
sub: Forty skiffs. Every one a souvenir stall.
open: A floating market: forty skiffs, and every one of them selling something you cannot use. They wave. They are very close. They have heard about you.

name: The Fog Bank
open: Fog, thick as wet wool, and the chart insists the river is clear. You can hear things. For the most part, they are the river.

name: The Low Bridge
sub: Three arches. The chart says four.
open: A stone bridge, a hundred years old and a good deal lower than advertised. The middle arch is a rumour. Mind your heads.

name: The Washboard
sub: Water that has lost its temper
open: Water that has lost its temper. Everything on the boat begins to rattle in a different key.

name: The Waving Island
sub: One tree. One man. He waves.
open: A tiny island with one tree and one man, who waves like it is his job. It is. He has been paid to wave since 1898.

name: The Cable Ferry
sub: The cable is at neck height
open: A cable ferry, the cable pulled taut across your channel, and a ferryman who is very sure it is your move.

name: The Butterfly Bank
open: A cloud of butterflies lifts off the bank as you pass, so many that for a moment the river is orange and the skipper is a little emotional.

name: The Kettle Rocks
sub: They boil, if you are patient
open: Two rocks stacked like a kettle and its lid. It has been on the boil, locals say, since before the river had a name.

name: The Pelican Parade
sub: Eleven pelicans. All of them in charge.
open: Eleven pelicans on a sandbar, standing in a line like a very patient jury.

name: The Washing Line
sub: Someone's whole week, over the water
open: A village has strung its washing clean across the channel. Shirts. Sheets. A flag that is plainly somebody's trousers.

name: The Bowing Statue
open: A stone figure the height of a church, bowing deeply to the water, as if it has just been told something.

name: The Lantern Village
open: Strings of paper lanterns across the water, and a village that stays awake for the boats. They are very well rehearsed.

name: The Otter Slide
open: A mud slide, and otters using it with total commitment. They do not look at the boat. They know you are watching.

name: The Heron Rookery
sub: They have your hats in mind
open: Tall grey herons in the dead trees, every one watching your passengers' hats and sandwiches.

name: The Bell Buoy
open: A bell buoy tolling in the middle of nowhere in particular, marking a hazard the chart does not.

name: The Old Quarry
open: A quarry on the bank, and a bell that rings before they blast. It is ringing. It is Thursday.

name: The Hot Spring
sub: Steam, and a boiler with ideas
open: A hot spring steaming on the bank. The boiler appears to have noticed.

name: The Rain Squall
sub: It came from nowhere. It is going there too.
open: The sky goes dark in a single breath, and the squall comes down the valley like it has been waiting for you.

name: The Golden Hour
open: The light goes gold and the river becomes a postcard. Forty cameras appear. They are all pointed at the wrong thing.

name: The Boat Graveyard
open: A bank full of hulks, every one a boat that thought it knew the way.

name: The Hermit's Dock
open: A man on a tiny dock, who raises one hand to the boat in what could be a greeting or a long-held objection.

name: The Singing Cliffs
open: Pale cliffs full of holes, and the wind whistling through them in chords nobody asked for.

name: The Sleeping Dredge
open: A rusted dredge, half sunk, its great arm lifted over the channel like a hand waiting to be asked a question.

name: The Fish Weirs
sub: Nets, and the people who mind them
open: Fishing weirs strung across the channel in neat lines. The fishermen watch you with the calm of men who are in the right.

name: The Floating Gardens
open: Rafts of vegetables drifting in rows, each with a tiny scarecrow in charge.

name: The Customs Post
open: A little customs post on a jetty, and an official with a stamp who has been waiting for you personally.

name: The Surveyor's Hut
open: A small hut on the bank with a drawing table in the window. Nobody has moved the pencil. You can see the afternoon he got everything wrong.

name: The Dragonfly Swarm
open: Dragonflies, thousands of them, and every one has decided the boat is the most interesting thing in the valley.

name: The Smokehouse
open: A smokehouse on the bank, a column of smoke going straight up, and a smell that softens a skipper's resolve.

name: The Drowned Steeple
open: A church steeple standing out of the water, the bell still in it. You steer round, and for the length of a breath nobody says anything.

name: The Rope Swing
open: Children on a rope swing, launching themselves off the bank, and a boat that is, from their point of view, a target.

name: The Tidal Bore
open: A wall of brown water comes up the river toward you, in no hurry, absolutely certain.

name: The Slow Barge
open: A coal barge the size of a village, doing two knots in the middle of the channel, and its captain has seen your boat before.
